segments.title: Part 2: Who's Next

tenBlocks.block3_goal: A five-shot, twenty-seven-second segment inside a two-minute animated comedy. Ben finishes his show-and-tell and Miss Park asks who is next. It ends the instant Mia's first line finishes — do not continue into her story, do not resolve anything, do not add an ending. The comedy is played completely straight. Nobody in frame knows anything is funny.
tenBlocks.block4_continuity:
Location: the room in @classroom, morning, throughout. Never leave it.
The camera stays on the same side of the action as in @location1 for the whole segment and never crosses to the other side. @Mia is on the right-hand arc and this never flips.
Ten children and one teacher, deliberate diversity, zero face repeats.
Costume is fixed for the whole segment and never changes.
tenBlocks.block6_visualStyle: Feature-quality 3D animated film, production CG, not photorealistic and not flat cartoon. Warm morning daylight, soft subsurface glow through ears and skin, tactile materials. Depth of field as a natural in-camera optical artifact.
tenBlocks.block7_cameraAndPerformance: Five shots separated by four hard cuts. The body plays broad. The face stays honest. No mugging, no pulled faces, no comic reactions. Anticipation: every move winds the opposite way first. Snap and settle with overshoot on arrival. Moving holds: held poses breathe and micro-shift. Overlap and secondary action: hair, cloth and attachments arrive a beat late. Eye life: micro-saccades, live catchlights, realistic blinks.
tenBlocks.block8_audio: Applause dying away, crayon scratching, small feet shuffling on carpet, quiet classroom room tone, subtle pizzicato strings.
tenBlocks.block9_exclusions: The only spoken words in the entire segment are the lines in braces. Nothing else written anywhere in this prompt is dialogue, and nobody speaks who is not named on a line. No extra cuts anywhere. No unison movement. No subtitles, no watermark, no logo.
tenBlocks.block10_maintainConsistency: Ten children and one teacher: @Mia, @Ben and @Miss_Park bound to their references. Children are 4.5 heads tall (long torso, short legs); @Miss_Park is 7 heads tall.
